In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the folding of rectangular bilayers on a substrate is a complex process, which depends on the aspect ratio, relative thickness and the extent of actuation.
the shape of the bilayer and the aspect ratio determine the rolling scenario, while the relative thicknesses of the layers and the adhesion of the bilayer to the substrate are secondary factors.
the folding behavior depends on a number of factors, namely the aspect ratio, the relative thickness, the actuation strain, the adhesion to the substrate and the presence of a substrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rolling behavior of the bilayers is governed by the aspect ratio and relative thickness of the bilayers.
shape programmed folding of stimuli-responsive hydrogel based bilayers is possible and can be achieved by tuning the aspect ratio and the relative thicknesses of the bilayers.
the folding of stimuli responsive hydrogel bilayers can be programmed by changing the geometry of the bilayer and its relative thickness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the folding behavior of stimuli responsive hydrogels is highly dependent on the geometry of the hydrogel, which can be utilized to design smart materials with desired folding properties.
the shape of the stimuli responsive polymer bilayer is a crucial parameter that can be used to control the folding of the bilayer.
by controlling the shape of the bilayer, the aspect ratio and relative thickness, one can control the folding mode and hence the resulting 3D structures.
